rules.rule: An employed worker quotes only the exact assigned step and current scope. Factory options come from the active original catalogue and cannot write that catalogue.
rules.initialization: Use the existing quotation and original development or adopted production step. The schema never supplies missing assignments or fictional suppliers.
rules.dateAndPermission: Record occurrence in the existing business clock. Every draft, submission and supplier read independently checks the assigned actor and active role.
rules.expectation: Signed worker selects an active factory and opens the exact board; input with a mismatched board, old direct price action, a fake external supplier on in-house and directory writes are rejected. Replay uses the same payload and request key.

rules.rule: Only the specifically bound approval actor receives an actionable submitted version and can decide it, with an independent database constraint.
rules.source: Approved workbench v10.1 §9.3 and §13.1; F03–F07, F11–F12.
rules.initialization: Reuse stable member binding/role and in-app notification receipts. Drafts create no approval todo and no employee or supplier is changed by migration.
rules.dateAndPermission: Verify current employed membership, the pending submission version and its bound recipient under transaction locks. Other owner and Root cannot approve or receive the same pending matter.
rules.expectation: Actual signed approval view and todo agree on the same item and version. Independent SQL rejects another approval actor and recipient. Return and later submission preserve original decision history.

rules.rule: Source publication, customer confirmation and budget commands jointly enforce current approvals while preserving unrelated manual and IE workflows.
rules.initialization: Require both table/column families for new writes. Infer no craft from missing historical fields. A pure development confirmation has no formal budget until the original formal order command.
rules.dateAndPermission: Retain original eligibility and lock ordering. The confirmation transaction checks current item, work assignment, version, approval identity and factory eligibility before writing a customer or budget fact.
rules.expectation: The staged 0300 fixture rejects enabled-only writes. Two valid 0301 approvals unlock the original confirmation and budget exactly once. The existing 16 customer/budget regressions preserve old sources, factual amounts, transaction boundaries, and historic snapshots.

rules.rule: Use existing scoped UI and original precise document identities for the craft centre, current and saved versions, without changing R5 IE navigation.
rules.source: Approved workbench v10.1 §9.2, §10.3, §11.3A and Appendix E DOC28.
rules.initialization: No new theme or global reset. Use existing signed sessions and reporting scopes; historical links select the saved revision rather than requesting a newer version.
rules.dateAndPermission: Current work and decision controls come from server authority; historic versions remain read-only and attachments are authorized against the saved step.
rules.expectation: Worker and bound approver complete actual browser actions. Safe recovery does not submit another version, older saved approval and attachment remain readable after a change, and original IE directory still works.

rules.rule: Publish the new storage and exact signed regression together through the repository’s existing release and gate path.
rules.initialization: Checksum-bound additive migration, no backfill, supported settings-browser and existing two-worker Postgres config. The two signed fixtures exercise 0301 and pre-activation 0300 in isolation.
rules.dateAndPermission: No effect on SLA or existing account bindings. Existing test resources are local, owned, and cleaned; no deployment access is used.
rules.expectation: Exact dated candidates are verified under the existing gate. R4 and R6 writes complete only on the jointly enabled schema; no new runner or lighter risk level.
